[model-manifold invariance] under an invertible change of parameters (Jacobian P): rank and nullity of g are unchanged (instances: rank 1 on the diagonal, rank 2 off it); det g is NOT invariant, det(PᵀgP) = det(P)² det g (generic 2×2, symbolic); hence the volume element √det g |dθ| IS invariant (change of variables)

[model-manifold invariance] raw eigenvalues of g are NOT invariant: F-C at θ = (1, 6/5) gives 0.001285, 0.36; after the change of units θ = diag(1, 10)θ′ they are 0.003487, 13.26, and the condition number moves from 280.2 to 3804 (cf. the nonlinear chart, CFT5e). Generalized eigenvalues of g relative to a second tensor h ARE invariant: eig((PᵀhP)⁻¹PᵀgP) = eig(h⁻¹g) (same characteristic polynomial), but they depend on choosing h, and parameter space supplies no canonical h

[model-manifold invariance] singular values of J are NOT invariant: at θ = (1, 6/5) they are 0.03584, 0.6 in θ, 0.03996, 0.6458 in log-coordinates, and 0.04871, 0.7233 under the prediction metric diag(1, 2, 3); they depend on both the parametrization and the prediction-space metric. The kernel is invariant: on the diagonal J(1, −1) = 0 and (W J)(1, −1) = 0

[model-manifold invariance] the length of a curve in parameter space, ∫√(θ′ᵀ g θ′) ds, is the same in θ and in log-coordinates (the integrands agree exactly) and equals the Euclidean arc length of the image curve Y(θ(s)) in prediction space (g = JᵀJ is the induced metric): for θ(s) = (1 + s, 2 + s), s ∈ [0, 1], L = 0.350545. Lengths are chart-invariant but depend on the prediction-space metric (the noise model)

[model-manifold invariance] the same model and parametrization with noise covariance Σ = diag(1, 2, 3) has metric JᵀΣ⁻¹J ≠ JᵀJ (magnitudes and eigenvalues are noise-model dependent); the null direction is not: on the diagonal JᵀΣ⁻¹J (1, −1) = 0 and the rank stays 1, off the diagonal it stays 2

[hyperribbon widths, 1-D illustration] the one-parameter model Y(θ) = (e^{−θ}, e^{−2θ}, e^{−3θ}), θ ∈ (0, ∞), is the curve (u, u², u³), u ∈ (0, 1); its extent (total length, the only width of a 1-D manifold) is the same in every chart (θ, λ = log θ, u = e^{−θ}: the speed transforms by the chain rule exactly) and equals 1.863023 (θ-chart quadrature 1.863023), but 3.9345441 under the prediction metric diag(1, 4, 9). Widths are parametrization-independent and depend on the ambient (prediction / noise) metric

[manifold boundaries] the boundary reached as θ₂ → ∞ is the one-exponential model e^{−θ₁t} whether approached in θ₂ or in λ₂ = log θ₂ (the limit set is parametrization-independent; only the approach rate depends on coordinates); the tangent direction of the removed parameter vanishes (∂Y/∂λ₂ → 0), and the boundary model's Jacobian has rank 1 versus rank 2 for the full model at (1, 2): the dimension drops from 2 to 1

[prediction space] for continuously indexed outputs Y(T; θ) = e^{−θ₁T} + e^{−θ₂T} in L²(0, ∞) (white noise per unit time), the metric is finite: g_ij = 2/(θᵢ + θⱼ)³, rank 2 off the diagonal and rank 1 on it: a 2-dimensional manifold. Its linear span is not finite-dimensional: any finite set of distinct exponentials is linearly independent (Gram det for a = 1…5 is nonzero). 'Function-dimensional ambient space' is justified once the outputs form a function with a stated inner product; the manifold's own dimension stays the number of identifiable parameters

[c vs model parameters] for finite c the form η_c = diag(1, −1/c²) equals Pᵀ diag(1, −1) P with P = diag(1, 1/c): different finite c are related by a change of units (R1), so the invariant content is the signature; the limit c → ∞ gives diag(1, 0), rank 1, which no invertible change reaches: a degenerate boundary of the family (C9b). The model-manifold boundary also drops rank (MMIg). Difference kept: the Lorentz allowed set uᵀη₁u = 1, u⁰ > 0 is one orbit of the boosts (homogeneous: (1, 0) ↦ (cosh s, sinh s)), whereas F-C's curvature varies (CFT5f): model parameters are coordinates on one non-homogeneous manifold, not structure constants of a form

[model image vs manifold] M = Y(Θ) is a model image (a set) in general. Cusp: Y(θ) = (θ², θ³) has J_Y(0) = 0 (rank drop) and a cusp at the origin. Node: Y(θ) = (θ² − 1, θ³ − θ) has J_Y ≠ 0 for every real θ (an immersion), yet Y(1) = Y(−1) = (0, 0) with independent tangents (2, 2) and (−2, 2): a self-intersection, so the image is not a manifold there although the rank is constant. Smooth-manifold structure needs constant rank plus local injectivity / embedding on the region considered

[parameters vs coordinates] θ ∈ Θ is a parameter value and Y(θ) its prediction. F-C: Y(1, 2) = Y(2, 1), so different parameter values represent the same prediction; rank J_Y = 2 at (1, 2), so θ gives local coordinates on the image of a small neighbourhood there (immersion, locally injective); rank J_Y = 1 on the diagonal, where θ is not a local coordinate system. The model Y = e^{−(θ₁+θ₂)t} has rank J_Y = 1 everywhere: θ never gives local coordinates, the identifiable combination θ₁ + θ₂ does

[Fisher notation] with J_Y = ∂Y/∂θ and Σ = diag(1, 2, 3), g_θ = J_Yᵀ Σ⁻¹ J_Y. For θ = θ(φ) = (e^{φ₁}, e^{φ₂}) with A = ∂θ/∂φ, the chain rule gives J_{Y∘θ} = J_Y A, and g_φ computed directly from Y(θ(φ)) equals Aᵀ g_θ A exactly. The matrix components differ (at φ = (0, log 6/5), g_φ ≠ g_θ entrywise); the tensor g is one object with two component matrices

[null directions: hypothesis] g(v, v) = vᵀ J_Yᵀ Σ⁻¹ J_Y v = (J_Y v)ᵀ Σ⁻¹ (J_Y v). With Σ⁻¹ = LLᵀ positive definite (L invertible), this is |Lᵀ J_Y v|² (checked for a generic 3 × 3 Cholesky factor), so g(v, v) = 0 ⟺ J_Y v = 0. Without positive definiteness it fails: with the singular weight diag(1, 0, 0) (only t = 1 observed), F-C at (1, 2) has v with J_Y v ≠ 0 but vᵀ J_Yᵀ W J_Y v = 0

[noise model: restricted theorem + caveat] (i) for g = J_Yᵀ W J_Y with a FIXED positive-definite W, ker g = ker J_Y and rank g = rank J_Y: on F-C, W = I and W = diag(1, 1/2, 1/3) give the same ranks (1 on the diagonal, 2 at (1, 2)) and the same null (1, −1). (ii) caveat: if the noise law depends on θ the Fisher information has further terms: for y ~ N(μ, s) with μ = e^{−(θ₁+θ₂)}, s = e^{θ₁}, the full Fisher information −E[∂²ℓ] = ∇μ∇μᵀ/s + ∇s∇sᵀ/(2s²) has rank 2, and v = (1, −1) has J_μ v = 0 but g(v, v) = 1/2. 'Null directions = ker J_Y' needs a θ-independent covariance

[volume element] det g_φ = (det A)² det g_θ, so neither det g nor √det g alone is invariant (F-C at θ = (1, 3): √det g_θ = 0.0137649, √det g_φ = 0.0412947 at the same point). The invariant object is the full element √det g_θ dθ¹ dθ² = √det g_φ dφ¹ dφ²: the volume of θ ∈ [1, 2] × [3, 4] is 0.003516358 in θ and 0.003516358 in φ = log θ

[width vs proxy] at θ = (1, 6/5) of F-C, the FIM eigendirections of different charts, pushed forward to prediction space (J_Y v and J_Y A w), point in different directions: rotated by 0.626° for λ = log θ and by 4.43° for the change of units θ = diag(1, 10)θ′. A width measured along 'the FIM eigendirections' of a chosen chart is chart-dependent unless the directions are fixed geometrically in prediction space; a width defined from the image set and a fixed prediction metric is not affected by this

[raw Hessian] for the cost C = ½|Y(θ) − Y(1, 2)|², the Hessian in λ = log θ is H_λ = Aᵀ H_θ A + diag(θᵢ ∂C/∂θᵢ): off the critical point (at θ = (1, 3)) the extra term is nonzero, so the Hessian matrix does not even transform as a tensor there; at the best fit θ* = (1, 2) it does, and H_θ = J_Yᵀ J_Y = g_θ (zero residual). Raw Hessian eigenvalues are chart-dependent proxies

[boundary language] (1) the parameter-domain boundary θ₂ = 0 of Θ = (0, ∞)² is a finite boundary point in θ but lies at λ₂ → −∞ in λ = log θ; the image limit e^{−θ₁t} + 1 is the same in both charts. (2) for Y = e^{−(θ₁+θ₂)t}, the boundary part {θ₁ = 0, θ₂ = s > 0} of Θ maps to e^{−st} = Y(s/2, s/2), already inside Y(Θ): a parameter-domain boundary that gives no new boundary of the image. (3) a model image of lower dimension than P has empty interior in P (the point (1/2, 1/4, 1/8 + ε) is off the curve (u, u², u³) for every ε > 0), so its ordinary topological boundary in P is its whole closure: not the boundary meant by MBAM

[image boundary stratum from interior points] F-C is symmetric, Y_t = 2e^{−st/2} cosh(t√(s²/4 − p)) with s = θ₁ + θ₂, p = θ₁θ₂, and s²/4 − p = (θ₁ − θ₂)²/4 ≥ 0 with equality exactly on the diagonal. In (s, p) the map has rank 2 at the diagonal point (s, p) = (2, 1) although J_Y has rank 1 there: near Y(1, 1) the image is the image of the half-plane p ≤ s²/4, a 2-dimensional piece with an edge, and the edge comes from the diagonal, which is interior to Θ, not from ∂Θ

[function-space example] g_ij = 2/(θᵢ + θⱼ)³ is the Fisher metric of the specific model Y(T) = e^{−θ₁T} + e^{−θ₂T} in L²(0, ∞) (MMIh), not a general formula: the model Y(T) = θ₁e^{−T} + θ₂e^{−2T} in the same space has the constant metric [[1/2, 1/3], [1/3, 1/4]]. dim P = ∞ (the exponentials e^{−aT}, a = 1, …, 6, are independent: Gram det ≠ 0; a Cauchy matrix for every N) while dim of the model image is 2

[limit-specific dimension drop] for F-C, θ₂ → ∞ gives the 1-dimensional face e^{−θ₁t} (MMIg) but θ₁ = θ₂ = r → ∞ gives the single point Y = 0; for Y = e^{−θ₁t} + θ₂t, θ₂ → ∞ has no limit in P (it diverges); for Y = e^{−θ₁t} + sin(θ₂)t, θ₂ → ∞ has no limit (it oscillates). 'Sending a parameter to infinity drops the dimension 2 → 1' is a result of the F-C example and that limit, not a theorem about parameters

[c: three roles kept apart] on (t, x), η_c = diag(1, −1/c²). Role 1 (representation): for each finite c, η_c = P_cᵀ diag(1, −1) P_c with P_c = diag(1, 1/c), a rescaling of x; this is a statement about the matrix representation, not about the physical role of c. Role 3 (theory family): lim_{c→∞} η_c = diag(1, 0), a degenerate limiting bilinear form (rank 1). Since det(Pᵀ η P) = det(P)² det η, no invertible change of representation takes a nondegenerate η_c to it: the limit is not a coordinate change inside one finite-c form. Its kernel is span{(0, 1)}: it gives 0 for every purely spatial displacement, so it does not by itself supply spatial distances (Galilean / Newton–Cartan structure needs more; not carded)

[named channel] the existing construction (W1d, W2a, W2b) uses D(ρ) = P_t ρ P_t + P_s ρ P_s, the non-selective projective measurement of total spin S² (P_t, P_s: triplet and singlet projectors), on ρ = |ud⟩⟨ud|, |ud⟩ = (|1,0⟩ + |0,0⟩)/√2. It removes exactly the off-diagonal terms ⟨1,0|ρ|0,0⟩ = ⟨0,0|ρ|1,0⟩ = 1/2 between the measured eigenspaces. S_z = 0 survives for a checked reason: [P_t, S_z] = [P_s, S_z] = 0 and S_z ρ = 0 give S_z D(ρ) = 0. It is not generic: the non-selective S_x⁽¹⁾ measurement on the same state gives Tr(S_z E(ρ)) = −ħ/2 ([Q±, S_z] ≠ 0)

[observation-type maps are different operations] projection Pₙ (n = 3): linear and idempotent on vectors (P² = P). Measurement channel D: idempotent on density matrices (D∘D = D), but D(|ud⟩⟨ud|) has rank 2 and purity 1/2, so D is not induced by any map on state vectors (ρ ↦ KρK†/Tr keeps a pure state pure). Marginalization: the joints [[1/4, 1/4], [1/4, 1/4]] and diag(1/2, 1/2) have the same marginals; it maps to a different space. Decimation RG: tanh K′ = tanh²K acts on couplings and is not idempotent (K = 1: K′ ≠ K″). A boundary limit is not a map on states (MMIg); non-identifiability is a property of Y's fibers (MMPb). Same questions, different operations: their unification is OPEN

but the state can change: for psi = |ud> (S_z = 0), the S^2 outcomes are P_t psi = A/sqrt2 and P_s psi = B/sqrt2, neither a multiple of psi; for A and B themselves (eigenstates of S^2) the state is unchanged

two exact zeros made of nonzero contributions: S_z^(1)X = (hbar/2)Y, S_z^(2)X = -(hbar/2)Y, S_z^(1)Y = (hbar/2)X, S_z^(2)Y = -(hbar/2)X; each contribution is nonzero and each pair sums to 0 (S_z X = S_z Y = 0)

obstruction: U = exp(i pi S_z^(1)/hbar) is unitary, commutes with S_z^(1) and S_z^(2), and maps X to iY and each contribution of X to i times the matching contribution of Y. So no descriptor built only from (psi, S_z^(1), S_z^(2), inner products), invariant under such unitaries and global phase, can separate the two zeros. U does not commute with the exchange P or with S^2

blind descriptor 4 separates them: with the canonical exchange P, P c1 = eps c2 gives eps(X) = +1 and eps(Y) = -1; eps equals the exchange parity of the state (covariance: P S_z^(1) P = S_z^(2)); with V = P U, which also swaps the summands, V c1 is a multiple of c2 for neither state, so eps needs the canonical identification of the two factors

reveal: S^2 X = 2 hbar^2 X (triplet |1,0>) and S^2 Y = 0 (singlet |0,0>); the pre-registered rule eps = +1 -> 2 hbar^2, eps = -1 -> 0 holds, through the textbook identity S^2 = hbar^2 (1 + P) (secondary existing mathematics, not project geometry)

domain of eps: |ud> also has S_z = 0, but it is not an exchange eigenstate; its contributions are (hbar/2)|ud> and -(hbar/2)|ud> (parallel to the state), and P c1 is a multiple of c2 for no sign, so eps is undefined there

restricted obstruction: U = exp(i pi S_z^(1)/hbar) acts on C^2 (x) C^2, commutes with S_z^(1), S_z^(2) and S_z, and maps the configuration C = (psi, S_z^(1)psi, S_z^(2)psi) of |1,0> to i times that of |0,0>. Hence every descriptor D with D(W C) = D(C) for all unitaries W commuting with S_z^(1) and S_z^(2), and D(e^{i phi} C) = D(C), takes equal values on the two; this class contains every function of the Gram matrix of C (norms, inner products, the relative cancellation c2 = -c1, spans up to such W). It does NOT contain descriptors using an operator that does not commute with U, e.g. <c1, P c1> = -hbar^2/4 vs +hbar^2/4

[Reduction | simplex projection Pₙ = I − 11ᵀ/n, n = 4] survives: every difference vᵢ − vⱼ = eᵢ − eⱼ; collapses: x and x + c1 have the same image (fibers x + span{1}); zero: Pₙ1 = 0, a nonzero source with zero image, and Pₙx = 0 ⟺ x ∈ span{1}; lost: the common component 1ᵀx/n; Σvᵢ = 0; not invertible (rank n − 1); compatible with symmetry: Pₙ commutes with permutations (R3). Reconstruction holds only under the orthonormal-source assumptions (G3b, G3n)

[Reduction | weighted centering C_m = I − 1mᵀ/M, m = (1, 2, 3)] survives: every difference (C_m y)ᵢ − (C_m y)ⱼ = yᵢ − yⱼ (relative positions); collapses: y and y + c1 (fibers y + span{1}); zero: C_m1 = 0, and C_m y = 0 ⟺ y ∈ span{1}; lost: the weighted mean mᵀy/M (R_CM); y is recovered from (C_m y, mᵀy/M). Its R3 role (commuting with D-isometries preserving span{1}) is CFT8c

[Reduction vs R1 | Fourier] the unitary DFT is invertible (U†U = I: lossless, R1); band-limiting P = U† diag(1,1,0,0,0,1) U is information-changing (P² = P, rank 3 < 6) yet commutes with the integer cyclic shift (equivariant, R3); keeping magnitudes only, x ↦ |x̂|, is invariant under the cyclic shift and many-to-one (the shifted signal differs, the magnitudes agree)

[Zero | PRESERVED ZERO vs COLLAPSED ZERO] preserved: under the Lorentz symmetry Λ (R2) the light-like v = (1, 1) keeps q_η = 0 and stays a nonzero vector (Λv = e^s(1, 1)); collapsed: under the reduction Pₙ the nonzero source 1 becomes the zero vector (Pₙ1 = 0). Different mechanisms: an invertible symmetry keeps a zero relation between surviving vectors; a non-invertible map sends a nonzero state to 0

[Reduction | wavelet filtering] a single zero-mean filter x ↦ x ⊛ ψ (ψ = (1, −2, 1), circular, N = 8) is not invertible: rank 7, the constant signal maps to 0; the filter bank (ψ, φ) with φ = (1, 2, 1)/4 has no common spectral zero, is injective (rank 8) and has an exact left inverse. Reconstruction belongs to a complete filter bank / wavelet transform under its stated assumptions, not to one filter

[Reduction | averaging] finite-scale low-pass averaging is translation-covariant, not invariant: (T x) ⊛ φ = T(x ⊛ φ) and |Tx ⊛ ψ| ⊛ φ = T(|x ⊛ ψ| ⊛ φ), yet both differ from the unshifted output for this x; the global (full-domain) average Σ|x ⊛ ψ| is exactly invariant under circular shifts. Local invariance at a finite averaging scale is a sourced theorem (Mallat 2012), not carded

[Zero | collapsed zero] the fiber over zero decides: for the injective filter bank, Φ⁻¹(0) = {0}, so a target zero implies a zero source; for Pₙ (n = 4), Φ⁻¹(0) = span{1}, so the target zero has nonzero preimages (a COLLAPSED ZERO). Not every target zero implies a nonzero hidden source

[Reduction | one channel on L²(ℝ)] the Mexican-hat multiplier ψ̂(ω) = √(2π)ω²e^{−ω²/2} vanishes only at ω = 0, a null set; so x ↦ x ∗ ψ is injective on L²(ℝ) (ψ̂x̂ = 0 a.e. ⟹ x̂ = 0 a.e.; Plancherel), although ∫ψ = 0. It has no bounded inverse: inf|ψ̂| = 0 (ψ̂ → 0 at ω = 0 and as |ω| → ∞). Zero mean alone decides nothing on L²(ℝ); the constant mode is not in L²(ℝ)

[Reduction | one channel on L²(ℝ), positive-measure zero set] if ψ̂_λ vanishes on a set of positive measure, the channel has a nontrivial kernel: with ψ̂ = 1 on π ≤ |ω| ≤ 2π and 0 elsewhere, the signal with x̂ = 1 on [0, 1) has ‖x̂‖² = 1 but ψ̂x̂ = 0 (so x ∗ ψ = 0 with x ≠ 0). The assumption is the positive-measure zero set, not zero mean

[Reduction | undecimated analysis bank, finite periodic ℂ⁸] x ↦ (H₁x, …, H_m x) with circular convolutions is injective iff at every DFT frequency some channel multiplier is nonzero: (1, −2, 1) with (1, 2, 1)/4 has no common zero and rank 8; (1, −2, 1) with (1, 0, −1) share the zero at frequency 0 and have rank 7 (the constant mode is lost). On L²(ℝ) the analogous condition is no common zero almost everywhere (stated, not carded)

[Reduction | critically sampled bank] perfect reconstruction needs an invertible polyphase system, R(z)E(z) = c z^(−K) I (type-1 convention H_i(z) = E_i0(z²) + z⁻¹E_i1(z²)), not the scalar no-common-zero condition: H₀ = 1 + z⁻¹ and H₁ = 1 + z⁻² share no zero and the UNDECIMATED bank is injective (rank 8 on ℂ⁸), yet after decimation by 2 det E(z) = −(1 + z⁻¹) vanishes at z = −1 and the decimated analysis map on ℂ⁸ has rank 7. Haar: E(z) is constant and invertible, R = E⁻¹ gives R E = I (K = 0, c = 1), and the decimated Haar map is orthogonal
